This petition has been filed for quashing of the entire complaint including the order taking cognizance dated 22.09.2009, by which, cognizance for the offences under Section 16(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with C-IV/13/09 (T.R. No. 1407/09), pending in the court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi.
3. Complaint case was filed alleging therein that the samples of alleged adulterated Cadbury Chocolate have been collected from the premises of one Ram Ratan Agarwal on 03.06.2009.

It is further alleged that on analysis, the Public Analyst, Ranchi vide his report No. 544, dated 27.06.2009, enclosed with prosecution report, has opined that the filled chocolate (Cadbury 5 Star)
does not confirm the standard of quality as laid down under the P.F.A. Rules, 1955 and as such, it was found to be adulterated by virtue of presence of hydrogenated vegetable fat.
4.

Mr. Agrawal, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the O.P. No. 2 has filed a complaint petition alleging therein that Cadbury Five Star chocolate was found adulterated is wholly without jurisdiction in the teeth of definition of 'filled chocolate' given in Appendix-B of A.25.03.

He further submits that Appendix-B has been issued under Rule-5 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. Rule-5 states that standard of quality of various articles specified in Appendix-B to the rules is defined in that appendix.
Appendix A.25.03 states about the standard of chocolate.

He further submits that the case of the main accused namely Pawan Kumar Agarwal @ Pawan Agarwal has already been quashed by this court in Cr.M.P. No. 196 of 2011 by order dated 01.09.2011 [reported in 2012 (2) JCR 395 Jhr].
On these grounds, he submits that entire criminal proceedings are bad in law and the same may kindly be quashed.

5. On the other hand, Mr. Shastri, learned A.P.P. appearing for the State submits that as per the norms prescribed in the Rule for manufacturing of filled chocolate, it is necessary for the manufacturer to coat 25% chocolate over the filled item.
Thus, the said chocolate content require to fulfill the norms prescribed for chocolate.
He submits that the norms prescribed for the chocolate clearly show that no hydrogenated vegetable fact can be used for its manufacturing.
On these grounds, he submits that the learned court has rightly taken the cognizance and no interference is required by this court.

6. In view of the above facts and submissions of the parties, the court has gone through the materials available on record as well as the relevant Sections and Rules of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and finds that the relevant Rules, Appendix-B Clause [A.25.03] of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 prescribed the content of chocolate.

From perusal of the said clause of Appendix-B, it appears that for preparation of filled chocolate, separate content has been prescribed, which reads as follows:-
"Filled chocolate means a product having an external coating of chocolate with a center clearly distinct through its composition from the external coating, but does not include flour confectionery, pastry and biscuit products.
The coating shall be of chocolate that meets the requirements of one or more of the chocolate types mentioned above.
The amount of chocolate component of the coating shall not be less than 25 percent of the total mass of the finished product"
7. From perusal of the standard fixed for preparation of filled chocolate, it manifest that use of hydrogenated vegetable fats in the center of filled chocolate is not prohibited.
8. From perusal of the report of the Public Analyst, it is clear that the sample in question is a filled chocolate.
Analyst only stated that hydrogenated vegetable fats found in the sample.
He did not say that the said hydrogenated fat found in the center of chocolate or its coated portion.

9. In view of the above, the standard prescribed for preparation of filled chocolate does not prohibit use of hydrogenated vegetable fat, thus, present of the same in the filled chocolate, cannot be treated as an adulterated food under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

sentences.text: Further from perusal of explanation attached to Section 2(ia)(m) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, it appears that if two or more articles of primary food are mixed together and resultant article of food is not injurious to health, then such resultant article shall not be deemed to be adulterated within the meaning of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The Public Analyst has not reported that sample of 5 Star Chocolate is injuries to health of human being.
Thus, on that ground also sample in question cannot be declared as an adulterated food article, selling of which prohibited under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

11. In view of the above facts, reasons and analysis and also considering that the proceedings of main accused has already been quashed, as such, to allow to proceed against the petitioners will amount to an abuse of the process of law.

12. Accordingly, the entire complaint including the order taking cognizance dated 22.09.2009, by which, cognizance for the offences under Section 16(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with C-IV/13/09 (T.R.
No. 1407/09), pending in the court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi, are hereby, quashed so far as this petitioner is concerned.
13. This petition is allowed and disposed of.
